auditPhase: Phase 14 -- UKIJ Diwani Tom (Debian 2011 snapshot) technical audit; APPROVED FOR PRODUCTION
methodologyNote: Every entry below was researched independently of alfont.com's own page content, per Phase 10B's explicit rule that alfont is a lead database only, never a licensing source. 'originalSource'/'authoritativeURL'/'license' are backed by an official project page, a Linux distribution's own package metadata (Fedora/EPEL, which requires legal review before a font is packaged as OFL), or a font-catalog site's structured license field cross-checked against at least one other independent source. No font file has been downloaded into this repository or into any audit directory this phase -- 'technicalStatus' and 'tashkeelStatus' are 'not_performed' for every entry because that requires an actual file, and downloading requires the user's explicit go-ahead, which has not yet been given. Where a candidate's authoritative status is now strong enough that downloading it would be reasonable, that is called out explicitly in 'finalDecision' as the recommended next step, not treated as already done. PHASE 11 ADDENDUM: Six fresh research passes were run against the same authoritative-source hierarchy (designer/foundry > official repo > government/institutional repo > reviewed Linux packaging > Google Fonts > FontLibrary-with-identifiable-source > other recognized sources), explicitly excluding Alfont, anonymous mirrors, and 'free download' pages as licensing evidence. Two candidates cleared the license gate for the first time this phase (UKIJ Diwani Tom, via Debian's own human-reviewed debian/copyright file; Bouazzi Maghribi, via its own GitHub README's MIT claim) and were then tested for real file acquisition inside this sandbox so the technical gate (fontTools/HarfBuzz/Tashkeel testing) could proceed. Bouazzi Maghribi's claimed license could NOT be corroborated at the file level (see its entry) and has been downgraded accordingly -- 'probably free' language in a README is never upgraded to a clean license classification on its own. No font file was added to assets/fonts/calligraphy/ this phase; Layla Thuluth (Phase 10D) remains the only font this project's most recent phase added to production.

candidates.name: Layla Thuluth
candidates.originalSource: The 'Layla fonts' project (a collection of traditional Arabic typefaces: Thuluth, Kufi, Ruqaa, and a Naskh-style 'BasicArabic'). The designer's own project homepage (formerly on Google Sites) is no longer live, but the font is currently packaged and distributed by Fedora Linux as 'layla-thuluth-fonts' (built for Fedora 39, a current release) and was previously packaged for CentOS 7/EPEL and Fedora 27 — i.e. it has been continuously carried forward as a legitimate distro package for well over a decade, which requires Fedora's own font-licensing review to have passed.
candidates.authoritativeURL: https://fedoraproject.org/wiki/Layla_fonts (project/package description); package itself distributed via Fedora's official repositories
candidates.license: OFL (SIL Open Font License) — stated on the Fedora Project Wiki's package characteristics table, and independently corroborated by FontLibrary.org's catalog entry for the sibling 'Layla BasicArabic' font from the same project
candidates.redistribution: yes (standard OFL term, and Fedora's own redistribution of the package is itself a live demonstration of this)
candidates.modification: yes, with OFL's standard reserved-font-name restriction (a modified build cannot keep calling itself "Layla" without the copyright holder's permission)
candidates.attribution: required — OFL requires the copyright/license notice to travel with the font
candidates.technicalStatus: PASS — Phase 10C independently audited the user-provided authoritative file (SHA-256 31d204337e70699a9a8c1461d737bd5f3cd1c283dad8970915222bac9c9bc74d, matching Fedora/FontLibrary provenance exactly): 459 valid glyphs, real GSUB with correct init/medi/fina/isol joining, no corrupt outlines. Structurally missing GPOS/GDEF/fvar/gvar tables entirely — the one genuinely unusual trait versus every other bundled font.
candidates.tashkeelStatus: PASS as of Phase 10D — Phase 10C found 9/12 marks genuinely supported but 3/12 (Maddah, Hamza Above, Hamza Below) falsely reported available (inserting a .notdef placeholder), and all 6 combined marks rendering fully overlapped, both traced to the font's total absence of a GPOS table. Phase 10D hardened the editor's own Tashkeel detection (real glyph-ID and cmap checks, replacing the advance-width-only heuristic) so the 3 missing marks now correctly show unavailable, and added a generic (not Layla-specific) editor-computed stacking placement for combos on any GPOS-less font, verified to produce correctly separated, non-overlapping geometry. See PHASE10C_REPORT.md and PHASE10D_REPORT.md.
candidates.calligraphyClassification: B — credible, genuine Thuluth-style calligraphy (Phase 10C's direct glyph-outline and rendered-comparison inspection): flowing joined letterforms closer in character to this project's existing Tholoth family than to its Naskh family. Not A: an independent/hobbyist FontForge release, not a vetted historical-Thuluth revival.
candidates.finalDecision: APPROVED FOR PRODUCTION (Phase 10D, 2026-09-05) — bundled as assets/fonts/calligraphy/laylathuluth/LaylaThuluth-Regular.{ttf,woff2}, registered as the "ثلث (Layla)" variation of the existing "thuluth" family in assets/js/calligraphy-data.js (alongside Tholoth), with its own embedded OFL 1.1 license text bundled verbatim as OFL.txt. All Phase 10D acceptance-gate items (A-L) passed; see PHASE10D_REPORT.md for the complete decision record.

candidates.name: UKIJ Diwani Tom
candidates.designer: Tursun Sultan (named on FontLibrary.org for the sibling 'UKIJ Diwani' release from the same foundry)
candidates.originalSource: Uyghur Computer Science Association (UKIJ) — a real, active institutional font project. 'UKIJ Diwani Tom' is listed by name (entry #64) on the project's own official fonts page.
candidates.license: OFL-1.1 or LGPL-3 (dual-licensed; this project distributes under OFL-1.1)
candidates.licenseURL: https://opensource.org/license/ofl-1-1/ (per Debian debian/copyright: OFL-1.1 or LGPL-3, blanket "Files: *" entry, re-verified directly against metadata.ftp-master.debian.org in Phase 14)
candidates.redistribution: YES, for the 2011 snapshot (fonts-ukij-uyghur_20110217.orig.tar.bz2, SHA-256 66bc43736d5f6e2e7ab1671bb0f708f2fa3b7a9182fb7036d46b3bab85a1d225 for the extracted UKIJDiT.ttf) -- the 2004 v2.00 binary remains separately REJECTED, unchanged, see below.
candidates.webEmbedding: YES, for the 2011 snapshot -- OFL-1.1 permits @font-face embedding.
candidates.modification: yes under either license option; OFL-1.1's reserved-font-name clause does not apply here since Debian's copyright file records no Reserved Font Name for this package
candidates.technicalStatus: Phase 12: fontTools + real HarfBuzz shaping completed on the actual attached file. Structurally sound for plain text: real GSUB init/medi/fina/liga joining, all 28 basic Arabic letters and connected words shape correctly with zero .notdef and correct RTL clustering. No GPOS table (same gap as Layla Thuluth). No fvar/gvar -- single static style, genuinely no variations. 1,070 glyphs, 229KB TTF. Phase 13: found that Debian's fonts-ukij-uyghur source package is actually built from a later upstream snapshot, fonts-ukij-uyghur_20110217.orig.tar.bz2 (SHA-256, per Debian's own .dsc control file, as retrieved: 47758bffb2da4e1ba8cc186f4be098e5e44fb0ac42a4b70ecdf49afd104d6d3 -- note this was relayed through a text-summarizing fetch tool rather than read byte-for-byte, so the last hex digit should be re-verified against the .dsc directly before being relied on) -- a genuinely different, later provenance than the 2004 v2.00 binary already audited and rejected. However, the package's full Debian changelog (versions 20110217-1 through -4, spanning 2011-2021) contains zero entries referencing any fix, update, or correction to Diwani Tom specifically -- the only font-specific change recorded is an unrelated font swap ('Tuz Tom' replaced by 'Esliye' in version -2). This does not confirm the tarball's copy of UKIJDiT.ttf is identical to the already-rejected file, but there is no positive evidence it differs either. The actual tarball could not be acquired in this sandbox (binary fetch is blocked here exactly as for the original file -- WebFetch confirmed it can reach the URL but returns only '[binary data]', no usable bytes). This remains open: a genuinely new, higher-provenance candidate that has NOT yet been technically audited, distinct from the already-rejected Fonts2u-sourced binary. PHASE 14 UPDATE: the Debian 2011 snapshot (fonts-ukij-uyghur_20110217.orig.tar.bz2, user-attached this phase, archive size 8,495,130 bytes and MD5 9c94757640bfeab3443ed7bd7894995b both matching the .dsc exactly) was acquired, extracted, and audited from scratch as a genuinely NEW candidate -- its results are not inherited from the rejected 2004 binary. The extracted UKIJDiT.ttf (SHA-256 66bc43736d5f6e2e7ab1671bb0f708f2fa3b7a9182fb7036d46b3bab85a1d225, 188,072 bytes) is confirmed byte-different from the rejected file via direct cmp, carries a different embedded version ("Version 3.00 November 4, 2010" vs. "Version 2.00"), and its embedded name-table license field reads plainly "LGPL" with a real GNU URL -- resolving the 2004 binary's unexplained "Alpsoft"/alplar.com conflict for this specific file (designer contact alplar@hotmail.com plausibly explains the naming coincidence). fontTools: 800 glyphs, GSUB/GPOS/GDEF present; GPOS is structurally empty (0 lookups/features) so Tashkeel combos use the honest editor-positioning fallback, never fabricated GPOS data; GDEF declares no Mark-class glyphs, so Tashkeel verification used direct cmap + shaped-glyph-ID validity plus independent BoundsPen outline inspection instead. No fvar/gvar/STAT -- static, single style; 9 non-standard "zz01"-"zz09" GSUB feature tags exist but are unregistered in the arab script's DefaultLangSys and are correctly inert (Variations: NONE, not fabricated). Real HarfBuzz shaping of all 28 isolated letters and all 8 test words/phrases is correct with zero unexpected .notdef. Diwani classification: B, from actual rendered shaped glyph paths, consistent with the 2004 binary's own design lineage. See PHASE14_REPORT.md for the complete 32-item technical record, including full editor integration, font-switching, save/load, export, mobile, and performance test results.
candidates.tashkeelStatus: Phase 12: FAILED -- 0 of 12 marks and 0 of 6 combos genuinely supported. All 8 basic Unicode Tashkeel glyphs (fatha through shadda) are structurally present (correct cmap entries, correct zero-advance metrics, correctly GDEF-classified as marks) but have verifiably EMPTY outlines -- confirmed by direct fontTools outline inspection of all 28 of the font's declared Mark-class glyphs, of which these 8 are the only empty ones. This is a real defect in the font itself (missing artwork), not a detection false negative -- the same generic Phase 10D hardened probe that correctly found 9/12 real marks in Layla Thuluth correctly found 0/12 here, with the correct specific reason recorded for every mark. PHASE 14 UPDATE: all 12/12 standard Tashkeel marks and all 6/6 shadda+vowel/tanwin combos are genuinely SUPPORTED on the 2011 snapshot -- a complete reversal of the 2004 binary's 0/12 (all-empty-outline) result. Verified two independent ways: the hardened Phase 10D HarfBuzz probe (glyph-supported/glyph-missing/notdef-rejected, never xAdvance alone) and direct fontTools BoundsPen outline inspection of all 12 mark glyphs, both agreeing every mark has real, non-empty, geometrically sensible outlines. All 6 combos use positioningSource=editor (the font has no mark/mkmk GPOS data), via this project's existing, unmodified generic editor-positioning fallback -- no missing artwork was ever compensated for or fabricated.
candidates.calligraphyClassification: Diwani-B (credible, design-consistent with the 2004 binary's own lineage) -- confirmed independently in Phase 14 from actual rendered, HarfBuzz-shaped glyph paths of the 2011 file, not inherited from Phase 12's classification of the 2004 file.
candidates.finalDecision: APPROVED FOR PRODUCTION (Phase 14, 2026-09-05) -- the Debian 2011 snapshot of UKIJ Diwani Tom (fonts-ukij-uyghur_20110217.orig.tar.bz2, extracted UKIJDiT.ttf SHA-256 66bc43736d5f6e2e7ab1671bb0f708f2fa3b7a9182fb7036d46b3bab85a1d225) passed every gate this project holds any font to: license (OFL-1.1/LGPL-3, confirmed twice, prior conflict resolved for this specific file), font structure, Arabic shaping, Tashkeel (12/12 marks + 6/6 combos, real outlines), Diwani quality (B), editor integration (27/27), font switching (16/16), save/load, exports (15/15, all 6 formats), mobile (35/35, 5 widths), and performance. Promoted to production as assets/fonts/calligraphy/ukijdiwanitom/ and registered in calligraphy-data.js as "ديواني (UKIJ Diwani Tom)". Full record: PHASE14_REPORT.md. THE 2004 v2.00 BINARY (SHA-256 f9e66eb66e42cf673ee01788bfa26ca499f1df4352afccb797a9a97a920ef464) REMAINS SEPARATELY, PERMANENTLY REJECTED FOR PRODUCTION -- this approval covers only the 2011 file and does not retroactively clear the 2004 binary, whose license-conflict and empty-Tashkeel-outline defects were never resolved and were never re-tested this phase.

candidates.name: KACST Farsi
candidates.style: general Arabic-script display (Nastaliq/Persian search bucket — not a claim that this is an authentic Nastaliq calligraphic style)
candidates.designer: King Abdulaziz City for Science and Technology (KACST), Saudi Arabia
candidates.originalSource: KACST's own institutional font-release program. The originally-cited official page (ceri.kacst.edu.sa/fonts.htm) is no longer reachable (DNS resolution failure — the domain/subdomain appears to be defunct). The font is currently distributed via Fedora ('kacst-fonts' package) and FontLibrary.org.
candidates.authoritativeURL: https://fontlibrary.org/en/font/kacstfarsi (current, reachable mirror of the institutional release); Fedora's 'kacst-fonts' package
candidates.license: GNU General Public License (GPL) — stated identically by both Fedora's package metadata and FontLibrary.org's catalog entry, with NO font exception mentioned by either source
candidates.webEmbedding: NOT VERIFIED — a plain GPL license on a font, with no stated font exception, is a genuinely unresolved legal question for any tool (like this editor) whose whole purpose is to produce user-created output (SVG/PNG/PDF exports) using the font: an unusually strict reading of GPL could argue that output is a 'derivative work' requiring the same license, which would be an entirely different, much heavier obligation than the OFL fonts already bundled in this project carry. This needs an actual legal read, not an assumption either way.
candidates.modification: yes, under GPL terms (copyleft: modifications must also be GPL)
candidates.calligraphyClassification: not applicable — KACST fonts are a general institutional Arabic-script family, not a named or marketed traditional calligraphic style; alfont's placement of 'Kacst Farsi' under a Persian/Nastaliq-adjacent search context does not make it an authentic Nastaliq font
candidates.finalDecision: WEB EMBEDDING NOT VERIFIED — real, traceable, currently-distributed institutional source with a clear license NAME, but that name (plain GPL, no exception) carries different and heavier implications for this project than its existing OFL-licensed fonts. Do not bundle without a specific legal answer to "does GPL on this font impose any obligation on documents/exports a user creates with it," and separately, this was never a genuine traditional-calligraphy candidate in the first place.

candidates.name: Muhaqqaq — no candidate found
candidates.finalDecision: NO CANDIDATE FOUND — one lead (a Google Sites page titled "Muhaqqaq Calligraphy Arabic Font Free Download") exists but is private/login-walled and could not be accessed or verified; MyFonts lists Muhaqqaq-tagged fonts but those are commercial marketplace listings, not free/open candidates. candidates.name: Rayhani — no candidate found
candidates.finalDecision: NO CANDIDATE FOUND — search returned only the Wikipedia article on the Rayhani script itself (historical/calligraphic background, not a digital font). No digital font project, free or commercial, was located for this style. Reconfirmed in Phase 11: one near-miss, a font/name 'Reyhaneh', was checked and ruled out as an unrelated personal name, not a Rayhani-style typeface.

candidates.name: Jali Thuluth — no candidate found
candidates.finalDecision: NO CANDIDATE FOUND — Layla Thuluth (above) is a plain Thuluth font, not specifically a Jali (large/monumental) Thuluth variant; the two are related but distinct styles and this audit does not conflate them. No dedicated Jali Thuluth digital font, free or otherwise, was located. Reconfirmed in Phase 11 with a fresh, thorough search: 'Jali Arabic Variable' (a plausible-sounding hit) was checked directly and confirmed to be an unrelated sans-serif family, a false positive on the name alone. No genuine Jali Thuluth candidate exists in this audit's findings to date.

candidates.name: Jali Diwani — no candidate found
candidates.finalDecision: NO CANDIDATE FOUND — no dedicated Jali Diwani digital font, free or otherwise, was located in this pass, on alfont or elsewhere. Reconfirmed in Phase 11 with a fresh search: Microsoft's 'Aldhabi' is proprietary (bundled with Windows/Office, not redistributable); 'JH Diwani' is a commercial no-redistribution release; a font sometimes labeled 'Diwani Letter' online has no identifiable authoritative source; DecoType and Google Fonts were checked directly and neither offers a Jali Diwani product. UKIJ Diwani Tom (above) is an ordinary Diwani, not a Jali (large/monumental) cut, so it does not fill this specific style.

candidates.name: Bouazzi Maghribi
candidates.designer: Alef Type Foundry (GitHub org 'aleftypefoundry'); the project is dedicated to the memory of the late Dr. Ahmed Bouazzi, described as a scholar of Arabic-language preservation, but he is credited as the project's inspiration/namesake, not stated as the digital designer.
candidates.originalSource: GitHub repository github.com/aleftypefoundry/bouazzi-maghribi -- an identifiable, named foundry account (not an anonymous mirror), presenting itself as 'an open-source revival of a classic Arabic font based on the Maghribi script.'
candidates.license: CLAIMED BUT NOT VERIFIABLE AT THE FILE LEVEL, Phase 11: the repository's README states 'Bouazzi Maghribi is an open-source project available under the [MIT License](license.md)', but this phase confirmed via direct fetch that no such file exists in the repository: raw.githubusercontent.com returned HTTP 404 for license.md, License.md, and LICENSE.md on both the 'master' and 'main' branches, and a plain LICENSE (no extension) also 404'd. The repo's own root file listing (fonts/, samples/, src/, .gitignore, README.md, contribution-guide.md, installation-guide.md) confirms no license file is actually present, and GitHub's own automatic license-detection sidebar -- which flags a recognized SPDX license whenever a real LICENSE file exists -- shows no detected license for this repository. The MIT claim is therefore prose in a README pointing at a file that does not exist, not a verifiable license grant.
candidates.licenseURL: None resolvable -- README link target (license.md) returns 404 in every case/branch variant checked
candidates.redistribution: NOT VERIFIED -- cannot be confirmed without an actual license file or a direct statement from the maintainer
candidates.technicalStatus: not_performed -- withheld pending license verification, per this project's standing rule that only license-cleared candidates proceed to the technical gate
candidates.finalDecision: REDISTRIBUTION NOT VERIFIED -- a named foundry and a plausible MIT claim are a better starting point than an anonymous mirror, but 'the README says MIT' is not itself a license grant when the linked license text does not exist in the repository and GitHub detects none either. Per this project's explicit rule ('never upgrade a candidate because it is probably free'), this does NOT qualify as SAFE WITH ATTRIBUTION on the current evidence. RECOMMENDED NEXT STEP: open an issue on the repository (or otherwise contact Alef Type Foundry) asking them to add the missing license.md, or ask the user to check whether a license file exists in a location/branch/release this sandbox's fetch tools could not reach (e.g. a tagged release's asset bundle) before treating this as licensed at all.
